obs: "I hold public faith so sacred, when once pledged either to citizens or to foreigners, that a violation of that faith is never to be inferred as even in contemplation, but when it is impossible to give any other reasonable construction to a public act."

"If, under these circumstances, the legislature had withdrawn the authority of the town to issue its bonds or had imposed new conditions upon the issue, it would have been an act of bad faith. If possible, we should give such a construction to the act of the legislature as would relieve the State from such an imputation."
United States v. Central Pacific Railroad

"the construction which the appellants seek to put on the second section of the act of May 8, 1878, would not only render that section a breach of faith on the part of the United States ... The construction contended for by the appellee preserves the good faith of the government"
"Of course, this court would hesitate to accept any construction of an act of Congress that would imply bad faith upon the part of the government."
